title.value: Considerations and recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group for preclinical diffusion MRI: Part 2 — Ex vivo imaging: added value and acquisition
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly stated at the beginning of the document, provided by the authors themselves.
title.quote: Considerations and recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group for preclinical diffusion MRI: Part 2 — Ex vivo imaging: added value and acquisition

analysis.description: The paper provides an overview of best practices for ex vivo diffusion MRI, focusing on experimental design, sample preparation, and MR scanning. It aims to enhance the rigor and reproducibility of ex vivo dMRI acquisitions and analyses.

type.justification: The paper focuses on providing guidelines, concepts, and recommendations rather than conducting experiments or empirical studies.
type.quote: This work does not serve as a “consensus” on any specific topic, but rather as a snapshot of “best practices” or “guidance” from the preclinical dMRI community as represented by the authors.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on diffusion MRI, specifically preclinical diffusion MRI involving ex vivo imaging.
name.quote: Considerations and recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group for preclinical diffusion MRI: ...

name.justification: The paper specifically addresses ex vivo imaging as a critical application area within diffusion MRI.
name.quote: Ex vivo dMRI is increasingly being used to probe tissue microstructure and brain connectivity.

name.justification: The text discusses the use of diffusion tensors in MRI, which is a core component of DTI.
name.quote: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI): as in in vivo, recommendations include 20-30 non-collinear directions to mitigate noise.

is_contributed.justification: The model is used within the paper but is not claimed as a contribution of this research.
is_contributed.quote: we recommend informing acquisition settings by acquiring scans prior to the start of a new study and optimize using methods described in the literature.

is_executed.justification: The paper does not perform actual MRI scans or experiments but discusses best practices for such procedures.
is_executed.quote: This work does not serve as a “consensus” on any specific topic, but rather as a snapshot of “best practices” or “guidance” from the preclinical dMRI community.

is_compared.justification: As a guideline paper, it discusses methodologies but does not compare empirical results of models.
is_compared.quote: Diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) and other advanced dMRI methods is sometimes challenging on postmortem human tissue due to the prohibitively high b-values required.
